newsitem.title: CANADA: Aber values diamond sample at US$63/carat.
newsitem.headline: Aber values diamond sample at US$63/carat.

text.p: Aber Resources Ltd said on Wednesday that diamonds in a 2,900 tonne bulk sample from the A-154 South kimberlite pipe at its Diavik property were valued at US$63 a carat, down from a previous estimate of US$67 a carat valuation based on about half the sample.
The Diavik project in Canada's Northwest Territories is 40 percent-owned by Aber and 60 percent by mining concern RTZ-CRA.
Aber said that 12,800 carats had been recovered from the sample. About half that amount was analyzed earlier this year by Antwerp diamond experts and valued at an average US$67 a carat.
The lower value was derived by statistical extrapolation of that figure on the entire sample and no further stones were submitted for valuation, an Aber spokesman said.
In addition, Aber raised the estimated tonnage of kimberlite contained in four pipes on the property to 36 million from 33 million. This was calculated to a depth of 400 meters.

Of 45 kimberlite pipes discovered at Diavik so far, four pipes -- A-154 South, A-154 North, A-418 and A-21 -- are the subject of a two-year, C$80 million bulk sampling and prefeasibility study due be completed in the fall.
A formal feasibility study is expected to begin in the fourth quarter.

All four pipes have undergone mini-bulk sampling to establish an estimated grade of diamonds per tonne. Two of the pipes, A-154 South and A-418, have undergone large underground bulk sampling to establish an estimated value of diamonds based on over 10,000 carats from each of the pipes.

Aber said sampling on A-418 was running on schedule and it expects to receive valuations on about 3,000 carats in June. The pipe has an estimated grade of 4.0 carats per tonne for an estimated 9.0 million tonnes to a depth of 400 metres.

A-154 South has an estimated grade of 4.2 carats per tonne for the estimated 12 million tonnes to a depth of 400 metres. Further grade information from drilling done at depths of 250 to 400 meters is scheduled to be announced in late May.
At A-154 North, mini-bulk sampling yielded 71.7 tonnes grading 2.2 carats a tonne. Recent drilling increased the kimberlite tonnage to 10 million tonnes.
Aber said no more testing of this pipe is planned because the upper one-third would be mined from the same open pit as A-154 South at minimal additional mining cost.
A mini-bulk sample of pipe A-21 produced 6.9 tonnes at a grade of 3.1 carats per tonne. The pipe contains an estimated 5.0 million tonnes to a depth of 400 metres, Aber said.
Five additional holes have recently been drilled. This material will be processed in April and the diamonds sent to Australia for cleaning, sorting and initial valuation.
